reasoning: Recent Montana Senate polling from established outlets and pollsters shows Republican Kurt Alme leading the race, with the most relevant publicly reported poll within the last 45 days showing him ahead by 12 points in a three-way ballot test and by 6-7 points in two-way tests. Because the current race includes a notable independent candidacy and no credible 2026 Montana presidential poll appears in the provided results, the best current read from the last 45 days is a Republican Senate edge of roughly R+12 in the most race-specific survey, while broader aggregates point to a slightly larger Republican advantage.

sources.name: Tavern Research poll (via Poll Tracker on X)
sources.details: Tavern Research poll of Montana likely voters found Kurt Alme at 49%, Seth Bodnar at 25%, Alani Bankhead at 24%, and Kyle Austin at 2%; in a two-way test Alme led Bodnar 51%-49% and led Bankhead 59%-41%.

sources.name: Independent Center Voice / Independent Leadership Council
sources.details: Independent Center Voice / Independent Leadership Council statewide survey found Alme leading the three-way Senate race with 36%, Bodnar at 24%, and Bankhead at 22%.

sources.name: GrayHouse
sources.details: GrayHouse polling cited in later reporting found Alme at 41%, Bankhead at 25%, and Bodnar at 17% in a three-way Montana Senate contest.

sources.details: Polling average page for Montana Senate showed an aggregate lead for the Republican candidate, listed as 44.1% R to 25.1% I, with a polling average margin of R+19.0.
